key_points.text: Issue 6 (July 2020) adds the use of the Version-4 (USLP) Transfer Frame; Editorial Change 1 (September 2024) fixes heading numbering in sections 2 and 6.

Proximity links are short-range, bi-directional, fixed or mobile radio links among probes, landers, rovers, orbiting constellations and relays, with short delays, moderate signals and short, independent sessions.
The Data Link Layer has five sublayers: Coding and Synchronization (specified in 211.2-B), Frame, Medium Access Control, Data Services (which contains COP-P) and Input/Output.

Addressing uses a triad: the SCID (source or destination, according to the Source-or-Destination Identifier), the PCID (selects one of two redundant receivers) and the Port ID (routes user data to logical or physical ports, including hardware command decoders).
The PLTU uses a 24-bit ASM and a CRC-32; idle data between variable-length PLTUs maintains symbol synchronisation.

Two data transfer services exist: packet delivery (packets with a CCSDS-authorised PVN, segmented and reassembled if needed) and user-defined data delivery (octets, not reassembled), plus timing services.

Sequence Controlled service is a go-back-n ARQ using the PLCW report and guarantees no loss, duplication or misordering within a session; Expedited service has no ARQ and suits upper layers with their own retransmission or spacecraft recovery.

A Version-3 Transfer Frame is a 5-octet header plus a data field of up to 2043 octets; the header holds Version (2 bits, value '10'), QoS (1), PDU Type ID (1), DFC ID (2), SCID (10), PCID (1), Port ID (3), Source-or-Destination ID (1), Frame Length (11) and Frame Sequence Number (8).
QoS '0' marks Sequence Controlled and '1' Expedited frames; PDU Type '0' is a U-frame (user data) and '1' a P-frame (SPDUs).
U-frame DFC ID: '00' integer number of unsegmented packets, '01' segment data, '10' reserved, '11' user-defined data.
Segmented packets carry an 8-bit segment header: 2 sequence flags ('01' first, '00' continuing, '10' last, '11' unsegmented) and a 6-bit pseudo packet ID; only complete packets are delivered.
SPDU types: Type 1 (directives, reports, PLCW), Type 2 (time distribution), Type 3 (enterprise-specific status reports of 0 to 15 octets).
The Version-4 (USLP) Transfer Frame may replace the Version-3 frame over the Proximity-1 C&S sublayer, with USLP taking over the Frame Sublayer functions.
MAC persistent activities (hailing, COMM_CHANGE and resynchronisation) repeat a directive until the expected RESPONSE arrives within a WAITING_PERIOD; their parameters come from the MIB.

Time tags are recorded at the trailing edge of the last ASM bit of every incoming and outgoing frame; collection is triggered by a SET CONTROL PARAMETERS directive, and time correlation itself is outside the standard's scope.
COP-P uses modulo-256 single-octet variables, with FOP-P variables VE(S), V(S), VV(S), N(R) and NN(R), and a SYNCH_TIMER that triggers resynchronisation when no valid PLCW arrives.
A Type 1 SPDU holds up to seven 16-bit self-identifying directives (Directive Type in bits 13-15, kept for compatibility with Mars Odyssey).
Annex C lists the Management Information Base parameters (for example Hail_Lifetime, Carrier_Only_Duration, Comm_Change_Waiting_Period) with the sublayer that uses each.
Security is left to layers above or below; SANA action is not required, and no patents are known to apply.
Mars Odyssey's convolutional code lacks the G2 inversion; its UHF CW beacon frequencies are 437.1000, 440.7425, 444.3850 and 448.0275 MHz, with 401.585625 MHz for the lander.
For symbol rates above 512 ks/s, projects interoperating with MRO's Electra radio should consider NRZ-L instead of Bi-Phase-L.

notes: PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate covers; the extraction has 166 PDF pages (registry: 165). The Document Control page footer is garbled in extraction ('July 2024' and 'September 2020' overprinted); the EC 1 row itself is dated September 2024. 'MIB' in this document means the Proximity-1 Management Information Base (annex C), not the SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base. Normative references cite older issues than the library holds: [2] TM Synchronization and Channel Coding 131.0-B-3 (library: ccsds-131-0-131x0b5 and ccsds-131-0-131x0b6ec1) and [7] USLP 732.1-B-1 (library: ccsds-732-1-732x1b3e1); [3] is the library item ccsds-320-0-320x0m7c1, [4] is ccsds-301-0-301x0b4e1, [H4] is ccsds-350-0-350x0g3 and [H5] is ccsds-232-1-232x1b2e2c1. The companion C&S sublayer (211.2-B) and Physical Layer (211.1-B) books and the Green Book 210.0-G-2 are not in the library. The running header reads 'Proximity-1 Space Data Link Protocol'. Annexes F and G are informative mission-compatibility notes (Mars Odyssey CE-505 transceiver, MRO Electra), not requirements. No individual authors are named.
